transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands - 2026-01-08 10:00 PST | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: All staff

[00:00] Moderator: Hey everyone, welcome to the January all-hands, thanks for joining. We'll kick off with Elena for a quick company update.
[00:15] Elena (CEO): Thanks, uh, good morning folks. Happy new year, um, first all-hands of 2026. I want to start by thanking the team for shipping the runtime optimizations last quarter — huge improvement on cost per token. We saw a, uh, roughly 18% reduction in average hosted cost across our curated models, which is really meaningful.
[00:35] Elena: Quick overview today: top-level metrics, Q1 priorities, hiring plan, product updates from Priya and Marco, and then we'll open for questions. Please drop questions in the Q&A channel.
[00:50] Marco (CTO): Quick numbers from infra: median p95 latency down from 420ms to 340ms for 2k token requests on the verified models, and tail improved with new batching heuristics and a few kernel swaps. There's still work at long sequences but progress.
[01:10] Jordan (Head Eng): To add, we rolled a KV cache prefetch in a canary and it's promising — reduces repeated prefix recomputation in streaming scenarios. Still early, some edge cases with cache invalidation to fix.
[01:27] Elena: Nice. On the business side — Samir?
[01:30] Samir (CFO): We finished the year slightly ahead of plan on ARR, and our gross margin improved due to operational changes. For Q1 we need to be disciplined: hiring only where it moves the needle. We'll prioritize SRE, Core Infra, and two senior SEs on the Dedicated team.
[01:50] Priya (VP Product): From product, Q1 is about three things: 1) polish network and private deploy UX (VPC onboarding), 2) rollout of Optimize recommendations in Console, and 3) stronger defaults for batching/caching so customers see cost wins without manual tuning. We're also going to improve the onboarding flow for Dedicated so sales cycles shorten.
[02:10] [02:10] Audience: (clap emoji appears in chat)
[02:15] Elena: On security, we've made progress on SOC 2 Type II evidence collection — big shout out to the security and legal teams — and ISO audit prep is on track. We're expecting a close on SOC2 by end of Q1 if evidence collection stays on schedule.
[02:35] Elena: Ok product deep dive with Priya.
[02:38] Priya: Hi everyone. Demo-ish: Optimize will now suggest quantization profiles and batching configs baked off real workload heuristics. We ran it internally on a mid-sized customer workload and saw a 22% cost reduction with negligible quality loss — that was with auto-apply off by default. We're adding an opt-in pilot.
[02:58] Priya: We're also improving the Dedicated autoscaler policy UI — customers asked for more predictable throughput windows and burst configs.
[03:15] Marco: A short note on Private: the VPC installer got a patch to support customers with stricter routing tables. We've shipped a new CLI that better validates customer network configs; the on-prem package still needs some work around hardware discovery.
[03:35] Audience question (via chat): "Any timeline for on-prem GA?"
[03:40] Marco: We are targeting late Q2 for a supported on-prem GA for a limited set of reference hardware. That depends on a couple of field tests.
[03:50] Riley (EM): From engineering execution side, please expect tighter ship cycles — we'll freeze feature merges two weeks before any official release and run more cross-team testing. That should reduce post-release rollbacks.
[04:05] Elena: On GTM — sales, we need to focus on three verticals this quarter: regulated finance, healthcare, and platform partners. Those buyers care a lot about Private/Dedicated and compliance, so align messaging.
[04:22] Jordan: Quick note — ops folks, when you file incidents, please include repro steps and workload patterns. That helps perf team triage KV cache behavior.
[04:35] Audience question: "What about pricing changes?"
[04:38] Samir: No broad pricing changes planned for Q1. We'll run experiments with commit-based discounts for Dedicated and new bundles for Optimize. We'll share the framework next week.
[04:55] [05:00] Crowd murmur, someone says "Can we get more docs on benchmarks?"
[05:05] Marco: We'll publish a benchmark repo with runbooks and spreadsheets. Jordan will lead that.
[05:12] Priya: Also, expect a new quickstart for the Console that highlights batching and caching toggles.
[05:20] Elena: Ok hiring — Samir?
[05:23] Samir: People plan: We need ~18 hires this quarter, concentrated in infra, security, and sales engineering. We'll open hyper-priority roles and also hold a couple of internal promotion bands. Managers, expect candidate pipeline targets in your inbox tomorrow.
[05:40] Elena: A note on culture — with growth we need to keep rituals that help cross-team knowledge sharing. We'll keep lunch-and-learns and a monthly postmortem reading group.
[05:55] Audience question: "Will there be more all-hands?"
[05:58] Elena: Yes, monthly leadership updates and quarterly full all-hands.
[06:05] Open Q&A segment — mixed questions: support SLA expectations, dedicated burst pricing, roadmap for embeddings improvements, community open-source contributions.
[06:25] Staff question (voice): "Is there an initiative to reduce inference variance between regions?"
[06:30] Marco: Yes, smart routing improvements are planned; we'll add region-to-region fallbacks and consistent kernel selections to reduce variance.
[06:42] Elena: Wrapping up — quick recap: share Q1 OKRs, publish benchmark artifacts, security to finish SOC2 evidence, people to share hiring plan, and teams to tighten release process.
[06:58] Elena: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and links. Happy to chat after if you have specific questions.

End of transcript.
